critical_steps: The positive operators A1 and A2 sum to T^{-1}.
The total controlled quadratic form equals <Uf,f>, hence has exact positive bounds.
The first pointwise mixed operator T A1 U is non-self-adjoint and has negative quadratic value -1/10.
Therefore the positive square root required by the source coefficient field is unavailable.
Under pointwise positivity and square-root measurability, the repaired analysis operator has norm at most sqrt(B) and its adjoint gives the synthesis operator.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact two-atom matrix construction and direct comparison with the source's positive-square-root definition.
integrity.unproved_limits: No classification of all alternative nonpositive operator factorizations or minimal measurability hypotheses is asserted.

scientific_limitations: The result corrects the pointwise square-root analysis/synthesis construction in Proposition 3.3 and Theorem 3.4; it does not deny existence of the integrated controlled frame operator.
The repair assumes pointwise positivity almost everywhere and measurable square-root coefficient fields; no weakest measurable-field condition is claimed.
The counterexample uses two atoms and finite-dimensional real Hilbert space, so it establishes a structural obstruction without addressing unrelated continuous-frame results.
title: Aggregate controlled positivity does not provide pointwise coefficient square roots
